[{"id":"f-exclusivity-587b1fd6","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Client. Section 2(a) grants only a non-exclusive licence and expressly confirms that Client \"is not obligated to utilize the License and is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise utilize any other\" comparable software or services (subject only to not infringing TrueLink IP and to the Section 10 confidentiality obligations) — that is the preferred position. Section 8 contains no restrictive covenant on Client, and the only exclusivity-flavoured language elsewhere (the non-exclusive licence of Credit Data in 8(d) and the \"solely and exclusively\" forum wording in Section 12) does not restrict Client's sourcing freedom. We note but do not flag Section 3(i), which requires Client to order a credit report from TrueLink for each borrower where underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface: that is a narrow condition on use of TrueLink's own Interface rather than a requirements or sole-supplier commitment, and Client remains free not to use the Interface at all. The cross-referenced Non-Competition Agreement is a separate document outside this review.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-8bf8b7ea","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, stipulated penalties or early-termination/minimum-fee charges payable by Client. Termination (§14) requires only a written notice with service continuing to the end of the following month, and non-renewal (§13) requires 30 days' notice, with no exit payment. Section 5 obliges Client to pay only fees for services actually requested (subject to a blank minimum monthly service fee during the term, which is an ordinary committed-volume charge, not a termination penalty), and the anti-spam covenant in §7 imposes no per-message charge on Client. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is warranted. Note for negotiation, not as a deviation: the monthly minimums in §5a are left blank and are carved out of Client's audit and dispute rights in §6 — we should confirm those figures and remove that carve-out under the pricing/audit rules.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-81a93eb2","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"No non-compete, exclusivity or field-of-use restriction binds Client anywhere in the Agreement, so the preferred position is met. Section 2(a) goes further in our favour by expressly confirming Client is free to acquire, develop or license competing software and services (subject only to not infringing TrueLink's IP and to the Section 10 confidentiality obligations). The only Client covenants (Section 8) concern legal compliance, access control, no misrepresentation of underwriting decisions and no spamming — none restrict the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The single reference to a \"Non-Competition Agreement\" in Section 8(d) operates as a limitation on TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data, i.e. it restricts the Vendor and benefits us; the licence-grant wording tying Interface use to Client's consumer-finance origination business is a scope-of-licence limit, not a restraint on Client's business, and is noted only for completeness.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-4c8b19a0","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 14 gives Client a unilateral, no-cause right to terminate on written notice, with services (and therefore charges) running only to the last day of the month following the notice month — roughly 30–60 days' notice, within our preferred 30-day band and well inside the fallback. No early-termination fee or penalty attaches: fees are invoiced monthly in arrears under Section 5(a) (invoices paid within 15 days of receipt), so there is no prepaid-fee exposure and the absence of an express pro-rata refund mechanic is immaterial here (noted, not flagged). On the other side, TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right: Section 13's early-termination triggers are Client breach/default (for cause), and the only other exit is a mutual 30-day notice of intent not to renew at the end of each one-year term — an end-of-term non-renewal right the fallback contemplates, exercisable equally by us, in a 12-month (not multi-year) auto-renewing term. The 30- rather than 90-day non-renewal notice is a minor sub-element and symmetric in our favour, so we would not spend leverage on it. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-25c40485","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"I searched the full agreement for audit, inspection, verification, records, books, monitoring and access rights and found no provision entitling TrueLink to audit, inspect or verify Client's usage, records or systems. Section 5/6 runs the other way: it gives Client (not the Vendor) the right to supporting documentation and to contest charges, and Section 2(e) gives Client real-time access to its own usage statistics and raw log files. Section 8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical mechanisms against spamming, but that is an operational control on the hosted Interface, not an audit right over Client's systems or records. Since no audit obligation binds us, there is nothing exceeding the preferred position (no more than annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access) and no reason to introduce audit rights against ourselves. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-f65d9023","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The agreement contains a governing-law clause (§26) selecting California law and a venue clause (§27) giving exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in San Luis Obispo County, California, with consent to jurisdiction and a waiver of forum objections. There is no arbitration provision, foreign or otherwise. California law with California courts sits squarely at the playbook fallback (preferred is New York law and courts in New York County), so this is acceptable and not redlined. Worth noting only in passing that the venue is the Vendor's local county rather than a neutral or Client-convenient forum; that is a minor sub-element that does not fail the fallback.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-indemn-87d7d530","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 12 contains a TrueLink indemnity, but it is limited to \"any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder\" (p0075). There is no TrueLink non-infringement warranty anywhere in the Agreement (section 9 warranties are Y2K-only; the only infringement representations run from Client at p0055), so breach-based indemnity does not reach third-party IP infringement claims against the Interface or related software. The Vendor indemnity therefore excludes IP infringement, which fails even the fallback position (Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions and remedies), while Client's indemnity at p0071-p0072 is broad and one-sided. Redline adds IP infringement (with Client Content/modification carve-outs), breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus a standard defence/notice/control procedure.","proposal":"Insert a concise TrueLink defence and indemnity sub-paragraph covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control and cooperation.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-657fe724","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The only cap in the Agreement (p0077) is one-way: it limits TrueLink's liability to 12 months' hosting and support compensation, while Client's liability — including under the very broad Section 12a indemnity — is entirely uncapped. A cap protecting only the Vendor with the Customer uncapped is walk-away territory under LOL-CAP, so the clause fails even the fallback (mutual 12-month cap with carve-outs). There is also no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages anywhere in the document. The redline makes the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, keeps indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap, and confirms Client's payment obligations are not capped liability.","proposal":"Make the liability cap mutual, apply it to the Agreement as a whole, and place indemnity/confidentiality/misconduct claims outside the cap.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-mfn-ead09424","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The only most-favoured-nation language in the Agreement runs in our favour: in § 6 (DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES, p0047) TrueLink — the Vendor — undertakes that its Hosting Services rates \"will not exceed that charged by TrueLink to any other party,\" plus a one-year price freeze. That is a Vendor-granted MFN benefiting Client, which the rule expressly welcomes and directs us not to redline. I checked the remainder of the document for a reverse-direction obligation: § 5 COMPENSATION (p0045) sets only Client's payment mechanics with no parity or price-matching covenant, and § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT (p0051-p0058) contains no obligation for Client to extend TrueLink terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers. Searches for \"no less favorable\", \"most favored\", and price-matching language returned no other hits. There is therefore no MFN burdening Customer, which meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer). No redline proposed. Noted only for the record: the Vendor MFN is limited to Hosting Services rates and has no audit or true-up mechanic to verify compliance, but that is an enhancement beyond this rule's scope rather than a deviation.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-d668eb14","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"Section 5a imposes a minimum monthly fee floor for Hosting and Support Services, so this is not the preferred \"usage/ordered services only\" position. However, it sits at the fallback: the term is a single 12-month period renewing annually (Section 13), and Section 14 gives Client an unconditional termination right on written notice, with services and fees ending on the last day of the month following the notice month (roughly 30-60 days). There is no shortfall charge, take-or-pay make-whole, early termination fee or multi-year lock-in, and no volume cap on Client's usage; the minimum period in Section 4 is TrueLink's commitment of programmer resources to us, which is to our benefit. Noted for commercial follow-up rather than redline: the dollar minimums in Section 5a and the month figure in Section 4 are still blank, and Section 6 excludes the minimum monthly fees from Client's documentation and dispute rights, so the figures should be kept modest when completed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-d7d9246f","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT","rationale":"The Agreement contains no employee non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binding the Client. Searches for \"solicit\", \"employ\", \"hire\", \"induce\", \"recruit\" and \"personnel\" return only unrelated hits (the § 7 unsolicited commercial e-mail provision, indemnity references to officers/employees, and the § 8(c) access-limitation covenant). The Client covenants in § 8 and the confidentiality provisions in § 10 — the usual homes for such a restriction — impose no hiring or solicitation restraint on us. This matches the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so no redline is warranted. Note only that § 8(d) cross-references a separate Non-Competition Agreement governing Credit Data use; that instrument is outside this document and should be reviewed separately if it contains personnel restrictions.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-4d0df6e1","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 13 (p0078) provides an initial one-year term with automatic renewal for successive one-year (not multi-year) periods, and either party - including us as Client - may stop renewal on thirty (30) days' written notice. That window is inside the preferred 30-day standard and well inside the 60-day fallback, and the 12-month renewal term matches the preferred position; nothing approaches walk-away territory (no window over 90 days, no multi-year auto-renewal). Two preferred sub-elements are absent and are noted rather than redlined: no Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal, and no express renewal price cap (CPI/3%), though p0047 freezes Hosting Services costs for the first year and adds MFN rate protection in our favour. On its material terms the clause meets the preferred position, so we do not redline it.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-addbb3a2","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT","rationale":"The only warranty TrueLink gives (§9, p0059-p0060) is a Year 2000 date-processing warranty. There is no warranty that the Hosting/Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, no conformance-to-documentation warranty for the Interface or related software, no compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty (those run only from Client, p0051 and p0056), and no repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy. Section 12 (p0076) then disclaims all implied warranties of merchantability and fitness, leaving the Client with effectively no substantive quality protection. That fails even the fallback position (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies). The disclaimer is prefaced \"EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT,\" so it does not swallow an added express warranty and no carve-out edit is needed; the minimal fix is to insert the express warranty and remedy after p0060. Redline validated ok:true.","proposal":"Add TrueLink professional/workmanlike and conformance warranty with repair, replacement or refund remedy","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-assign-0ba91216","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 15 is the only assignment provision in the Agreement. It bars assignment by either party absent the other's prior written approval, with the sole exception of an assignment to a \"financially responsible affiliate.\" It therefore fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) there is no successor/M&A carve-out, so a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of Client's assets would require TrueLink's consent — the playbook treats a Customer assignment restriction with no M&A carve-out as walk-away territory; and (ii) the consent standard is unqualified, not \"not to be unreasonably withheld,\" so TrueLink may refuse arbitrarily (including on our affiliate transfers, where \"financially responsible\" is itself a judgment call). There is no competitor restriction on TrueLink's side. On the positive side, no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right exists anywhere in the document (searches for \"change of control\" and \"merger\" returned nothing, and the term/termination provisions at Sections 13-14 contain no such trigger), so only the assignment carve-outs need fixing. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, subjects TrueLink's assignment to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and bars assignment to a Client competitor, and confirms that a Client change of control is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no exit.","proposal":"Carve out Client affiliate/successor assignments, add reasonableness and no-competitor limits on TrueLink assignments, and confirm no TrueLink termination right on Client change of control.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-insurance-1c661cbc","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"A full-text search for \"insurance\" returns no results, and the miscellaneous provisions (Sections 13-30) contain no insurance covenant. TrueLink hosts the Client web site, operates the Interface and processes Client Content and consumer credit data, so it is exactly the type of vendor the playbook expects to carry coverage; no insurance at all for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory under the rule. We inserted a new Section 31 at the preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request), placed after Force Majeure so existing numbering and the Section 24 survival reference are undisturbed, and offered the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback in the comment.","proposal":"Insert insurance covenant requiring TrueLink to maintain CGL, E&O, cyber and workers' compensation coverage with certificates on request.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-51000819","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The only ownership provision is Section 2(d), which preserves TrueLink's rights in the Interface (acceptable under the rule) but says nothing about our side. No clause anywhere confirms that Client retains title to Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property (a defined term at p0012 that is never operative) or borrower/loan data, and nothing addresses ownership of the results of the Support Services we pay for. Section 10(b)/(c) only makes Client's IP and \"all results of the Hosting and Support Services\" confidential, which is not ownership, and p0078 addresses domains and Client Content only on discontinuance of hosting. That leaves the rule's preferred and fallback positions unmet, so we insert a reciprocal ownership subsection with a licence back for any embedded TrueLink IP and an express no-joint-ownership statement. Noted but not separately flagged: Section 8(d) grants TrueLink a broad non-exclusive licence over the narrowly defined Credit Data (raw, aged repository data excluding Client Proprietary Information), which is a licence rather than an assignment and is limited by the Non-Competition Agreement; our insert is expressed to be subject to it.","proposal":"Add Client ownership of Client Content, Client IP and borrower data plus assignment of Support Services deliverables and work product, with a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded TrueLink IP and no joint ownership.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-license-3bb56241","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The grant in Section 2(a) runs to Client alone; neither affiliates nor contractors acting on Client's behalf are licensed, and the scope provisions (2(b)) only add multi-site access, giving no path to extend use to group companies or outsourced providers. That fails even the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice). The licence is not expressly revocable at will — it runs until termination of the Agreement (2(c)) — so that limb is acceptable, but the assignment clause (Section 15) permits transfer only to an affiliate, not to a successor in an M&A transaction, which is also part of the fallback. Redline adds affiliates and contractors to the grant and successor transfer to Section 15; the shortcomings on perpetuity/irrevocability of paid-up licences are noted but not pressed given the subscription-style hosting bargain.","proposal":"Cover Client's affiliates on written notice and permit transfer to a Client M&A successor","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-transition-2aa5a23a","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"This is a hosting agreement in which TrueLink holds Client Content and borrower/loan data, but neither the Term (Section 13) nor Termination (Section 14) provision, nor the Confidentiality section (Section 10), gives Client any exit rights. Section 13 only puts the burden on Client to arrange a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, and Section 14 merely runs services to month-end; there is no obligation on TrueLink to provide transition assistance, to return or export Client data in a usable format, or to delete it afterwards. No such clause exists anywhere in the document, so the rule's expected clause is missing (below even the fallback of 90 days' assistance plus 30-day export). We propose inserting the preferred language as new Section 14a, which will survive termination under Section 24.","proposal":"Insert Section 14a requiring transition assistance, return of Client data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion.","verification":"repaired"}]

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Interface and Support Agreement)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings, deviations and next steps

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed EXHIBIT 10.4 against the playbook and produced 18 verified findings.
